title: seed_manifest

$schema.description: JSON Schema URI identifying the schema this seed manifest conforms to.

seed_manifest_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this seed manifest instance. Convention: {product-or-repo-slug}-seed-manifest. Examples: 'billing-api-seed-manifest', 'customer-portal-seed-manifest', 'devspec-toolkit-seed-manifest'. Should match the host repository name. Anti-pattern: 'seed-manifest-v1' (too generic) or using a version suffix here — version the manifest via the 'version' field.

version.description: SemVer string (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) for the seed manifest format. Increment MINOR when adding new seeds; increment MAJOR for breaking structural changes.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime when this seed manifest was initially created. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.

last_updated.description: ISO 8601 datetime of the most recent modification to this manifest. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Update whenever seeds or step_requirements change.

global_seed_order.description: Defines the canonical READ ORDER for seeds. It does NOT by itself cause a seed to be ingested at any step — per-step inclusion is governed by step_requirements[NN]. When a step's required seeds are resolved they are emitted in this order; required seeds absent from this list are appended afterward. Should include at minimum the IDs for the host's declared seed files.

seed_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this seed document. Should be referenced by step_requirements (which routes the seed to steps) and may also appear in global_seed_order (which governs read order only); seed-lint validates these references. Example: 'seed-overview', 'seed-tech-stack'. Convention: use the filename stem in kebab-case.

path.description: File path to the seed document relative to the repository root. Example: 'docs/seed/seed_overview.md'.

description.description: What this seed file contains. Helps prompts understand whether to prioritize this seed for their step. Write from the prompt's perspective: what will it learn from this seed? Example: 'High-level product overview, goals, and user personas. Read first for all steps.' Avoid vague summaries like 'overview doc'.

required.description: Whether this seed document must be present for pipeline execution. true: pipeline will error if this file is missing. false: seed is optional and prompts may skip it when absent.

source_type.description: Category of the seed source. 'doc': narrative documentation (PRDs, meeting notes, design docs) — prose documents that are human-readable only. 'spec': formal specification or schema — JSON, YAML, or CSV files that can be parsed programmatically. 'config': project configuration or environment settings. 'other': any source not fitting the above categories. When a document is both narrative and machine-parseable, prefer 'spec' if it has a defined schema, or 'doc' if it is primarily human-authored prose. Anti-pattern: classifying a plaintext changelog as 'spec' — it must have a parseable format (JSON/YAML/CSV) to qualify.

hash.description: Optional SHA-256 content hash of the seed file at manifest-update time, in 'sha256:<hex>' format as written by the seed-index tooling. Populated to let downstream validators detect whether a seed has changed since the manifest was last refreshed.

version.description: Optional version identifier for the seed document (semver like '1.2.0', a date like '2026-04-01', or a revision like 'rev-42'). Track this when the seed has an explicit author-maintained version. Distinct from `hash` — version is an author intent, hash is a verifiable content fingerprint.

items.description: Definition of a single seed document: its location, type, and role in the pipeline.

seeds.description: Registry of all seed files available for this project. Each entry describes a seed file's purpose and scope. Seeds are source-of-truth documents (PRDs, technical specs, meeting notes) that ground AI outputs in project reality. Must contain at least one entry; each seed_id here should be referenced by step_requirements (routing) and may also appear in global_seed_order (read order only), validated by seed-lint.

^(\\d{2}[a-c]?)$.description: Array of seed IDs required for the pipeline step identified by the parent key. Each seed ID must match a seeds[*].seed_id value in this manifest. Example key-value pair: '04': ['seed-overview', 'seed-tech-stack'] (FR list step requires both seeds). For multi-part steps use the full step key: '16a': ['seed-overview', 'seed-tech-stack', 'seed-domain-model']. Anti-pattern: key format '4' instead of '04' — step keys must be zero-padded two-digit strings, or the full step identifier for multi-part steps (e.g., '16a', '16b').

step_requirements.description: Mapping from pipeline step IDs to the seed files required by that step. Each step's AI prompt uses this to know which seed files to ingest. Key: step ID matching the pattern NN or NNx (e.g., '04', '05', '16a'). Value: array of seed IDs from the seeds registry. This is the authoritative inclusion set — only seeds listed here are ingested at a step. Steps with no entry (or an empty array) require no seeds — there is no fallback to global_seed_order, which governs read order only.

doc_paths.description: Array of glob patterns identifying documentation files in the repository that the step_16 docs_impact validator monitors. Use forward-slash glob syntax relative to the repository root. Examples: ['docs/**/*.md', 'README.md', 'api-reference/**/*.yaml', 'guides/*.md']. Anti-pattern: absolute paths or OS-specific separators ('docs\*.md') — use forward-slash glob syntax only. Anti-pattern: listing individual files when a glob covers them ('README.md', 'SETUP.md' → use '*.md' at the root level instead).

description: Schema for the seed manifest defining seed documents, their ordering, and step requirements.
